_comment: Freedom-of-information and declassified-archive sources the spider can read, by jurisdiction.
Built 24 Oct 2026 from three research passes; every entry was probed through the spider and ledgered.
probe.result: ok | refused (401/403/429) | robots (disallowed) | decoy (a 200 that is a refusal, a JS shell or a homepage-for-every-id) | not_found | unreachable.
A refused, robots or decoy source is recorded so the gap is visible; it is never worked around. Nothing here files a request, registers for a key, or uses a browser.
search/api templates take {q}. Run: python3 scripts/spider/spider.py foi list|probe|search|find --help
Human notes and the quotes behind each entry: research/sources/FOI-SOURCES.md and research/sources/foi/*.md.

sources.name: Lei nº 12.527, de 18 de novembro de 2011 (Lei de Acesso à Informação), texto atualizado, Câmara dos Deputados
sources.terms: official legislative database; reuse terms not read. robots.txt disallows search/form paths and individual deputies' pages, not /legin/
sources.use: Full current text. Art. 21 (sole paragraph): information on human-rights violations by public agents or on their orders 'cannot be the object of access restriction'; Art. 24: maximum classification periods 25 (ultra-secret), 15 (secret), 5 (reserved) years; Art. 35 creates the Joint Commission for Reassessment of Information (CMRI), which reviews secret and ultra-secret classifications.
sources.limits: Planalto's own copy (https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2011-2014/2011/lei/l12527.htm) could not be reached from this session (transport error 'ProxyError', ledger row 02:44 UTC), so this is the Câmara's copy. The law names no intelligence service; the exemption is by classification, not by agency. Art. 31 limits personal information to 100 years regardless of classification.
